# The Desk Has Limits {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #FF7A5C, #1C355E)"}

The context window

## Why Long Chats "Forget" {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="window" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
The brain's desk has a **fixed size**. You can only fit so many pages on it at once.
Pile on too much and **older pages fall off the edge**.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
That's the **context window** — and it's why a long conversation starts losing the
thread from the beginning.
:::

## Saved Beats Re-Pasted {auto-animate=true}

::: {.callout-tip}
## The rule
**Saved instructions beat re-pasting.**
:::

The app puts the important pages back on the desk for you **every time**, so they never
fall off the edge.

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-style: italic; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
This is the whole reason standing instructions, projects, and memory exist.
:::
